data.narrative:
Westmag is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Hansen and Jordan Sanders that has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including peers such as Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $11M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement in the sector. This approach yields an implied valuation of $28M. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow robotics manufacturing category—while 11 same-sector peers exist broadly, filtering for stage and valuation tier returned fewer than three datapoints, making a narrowly-filtered median unreliable.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $23M to $32M, with a median of $28M. This analysis reflects a single applicable method and should be treated accordingly. Key uncertainties include the limited peer comparability at seed stage in this sector and the reliance on raised capital as a valuation proxy. Additional datapoints at early fundraising rounds would refine this range materially.
